dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Ah, Aria. It seems you've already chosen a "human" form for yourself as well.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Hehe, you look just like I thought you might, Canon.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: That said, I didn't expect that you would proactively create such a form for those lovely little beings.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: It is only natural, Aria. Those fragile lives trust me and call out to me, so I shall respond to their voices.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: We were born to preserve the world. If the beings known as "humans" are willing to settle it, listening to their pleas fulfills the mission our King bestowed upon us.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Yes. After all, he did say that all life across the sea of stars are allies. They fight alongside us against the darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: But I wasn't talking about that. I mean, I didn't expect you, the "Frost Moon," to have such a sentimental side. It's endearing.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...I can see your language has already begun to be influenced by those small humans, Aria.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Their words are always so ambiguous. Do not use them. I cannot comprehend what you are trying to convey by saying "endearing."

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Oh, come on now!

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Sisters, shouldn't the first thing we do after shaping these bodies for ourselves be to sneak out and play with the people on the surface?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Otherwise, we'll have made them for nothing! Hurry, before anyone discovers us—

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Hehe. It seems our dear sister simply cannot wait, Canon.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Why, I remember that when they first started building their civilization on the surface, you even said, "That outsider is bad news, and naturally, its creations are the same." You wouldn't even spare them a glance.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Th—That's a different matter!

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: I still think you two shouldn't have let that outsider in, but the people on the surface...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Hah... As long as you have fun. Go on, and remember to stay close to Aria.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Huh? Aren't you coming with us, Canon?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: That Descender's servant said they had matters to discuss with me about this world's gravitational potential and metric ten{RUBY#[D]laws of time}sor.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Istaroth?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: I believe that was her name.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: You really should remember people's names, Sister.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: And perhaps it's just my imagination, but I have a certain... feeling about how she views that Descender...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: I won't jump to conclusions, Aria. But I'll keep an eye out.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: That's good to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's nothing. We'll go on ahead then, Canon.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Sonnet and I will bring you back a gift.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...I don't need gifts. Just be careful not to be recognized.
